sources.speaker: Iaroslav Amerkhanov

claims_used.claim: The speaker reported a 6% to 8% increase in menu-to-cart conversion after adding an image to a product in an A/B test.
claims_used.locator: Transcript: What About the Results?; browser text L283
do_not_infer: Paid-order conversion or sales increased by 6% to 8%
The figure is an increase of 6 to 8 percentage points
Refunds, repeat purchase or net profit improved
The result generalizes to a Chinese restaurant or platform

claims_used.claim: Regional content expertise was used to select images in the MVP workflow.
claims_used.locator: Transcript: How the MVP Was Built; browser text L222

claims_used.claim: The speaker recommended measuring generative-system quality before optimizing the generative component.
claims_used.locator: Transcript: Key Takeaways; browser text L289

unreported_in_reviewed_transcript: Whether 6% to 8% means a relative lift or an absolute percentage-point change
Paid-order, refund, review, retention or net-profit outcomes

author_analysis: Filling an information gap and demonstrating an AI advantage are distinct hypotheses.
A comparison against missing images does not isolate AI-specific value over real photography.
Production efficiency and restaurant operating gains should be assessed separately.
author_recommendations_not_test_results: Where permitted and technically feasible, compare initially missing images, real photography and AI-assisted editing of the same real dish.
Keep ingredients, portion, pricing, promotions and selling conditions consistent; do not create a misleading portrayal.
Prefer concurrent randomized assignment when supported. Nonrandom time comparisons are directional only and require recording possible confounders.
Predefine qualified exposure, an observation window, insufficient-data treatment and a stop condition for image–dish mismatch complaints.
Use consistent exposure, cart, payment and post-purchase outcome definitions across groups, with equal follow-up windows.
Track production and review labor separately from paid-order economics.
limitations: No new sales, profit or statistical estimates calculated.
Applicability to Chinese restaurants and platforms is unknown.
Current platform requirements require separate verification; the article makes no legal determination.
No inference is drawn from SSRN 6711039 or unavailable Meituan policy pages.
